paths.title: Planning & Task Decomposition
paths.description: Break ambitious requests into ordered, independently verifiable slices that reduce agent drift and integration risk.

lessons.title: Plan around outcomes
lessons.principle: A plan should describe completed behavior, not only file edits.
lessons.practice: Name the user or system capability delivered by each step.

lessons.title: Find dependencies first
lessons.principle: Some changes must precede others because interfaces, schemas, or infrastructure depend on them.
lessons.practice: Order work by dependency and avoid parallel changes that rely on unstable contracts.

lessons.title: Create vertical slices
lessons.principle: End-to-end slices reveal integration problems earlier than layer-by-layer bulk work.
lessons.practice: Implement a narrow path through UI, API, and data when feasible before expanding coverage.

lessons.title: Separate discovery from execution
lessons.principle: Unknown architecture or reproduction steps make plans speculative.
lessons.practice: Perform targeted investigation before committing to implementation steps.

lessons.title: Identify risky steps
lessons.principle: Migrations, auth, billing, permissions, and destructive operations deserve dedicated attention.
lessons.practice: Mark high-risk steps and attach stronger validation or rollback requirements.

lessons.title: Define checkpoints
lessons.principle: Long agent runs need points where assumptions can be revalidated.
lessons.practice: Pause after schema, architecture, or behavioral milestones to inspect the state.

lessons.title: Keep steps independently testable
lessons.principle: A step that cannot be validated creates hidden debt for later stages.
lessons.practice: Associate each plan item with a concrete check or observable result.

lessons.title: Limit simultaneous change dimensions
lessons.principle: Changing architecture, behavior, dependencies, and styling at once complicates diagnosis.
lessons.practice: Hold unrelated dimensions stable while implementing the primary change.

lessons.title: Plan data migrations separately
lessons.principle: Persistent data evolves on a different risk profile than application code.
lessons.practice: Design expand-migrate-contract phases for zero-downtime or reversible rollout where needed.

lessons.title: Plan compatibility transitions
lessons.principle: Consumers may not upgrade simultaneously.
lessons.practice: Use additive interfaces and staged removal rather than breaking all callers in one step.

lessons.title: Plan fallback behavior
lessons.principle: External services and optional capabilities fail.
lessons.practice: Specify degraded modes, retries, feature disabling, and user messaging.

lessons.title: Plan testing layers
lessons.principle: Different defects need different test scopes.
lessons.practice: Assign pure logic to unit tests, boundaries to integration tests, and user journeys to end-to-end tests.

lessons.title: Plan observability before launch
lessons.principle: Instrumentation added after an incident is too late.
lessons.practice: Include metrics, logs, traces, and alert thresholds in the implementation plan.

lessons.title: Plan documentation updates
lessons.principle: Behavior changes that are undocumented create support and maintenance costs.
lessons.practice: Identify README, API, runbook, architecture, or user documentation that must change.

lessons.title: Plan cleanup explicitly
lessons.principle: Temporary flags and compatibility branches often become permanent.
lessons.practice: Create removal conditions and follow-up items for transitional code.

lessons.title: Use issue-sized work units
lessons.principle: Huge tasks are hard for both agents and reviewers to reason about.
lessons.practice: Split work so each PR has one coherent purpose and manageable diff.

lessons.title: Parallelize only independent tasks
lessons.principle: Concurrent agents can overwrite assumptions or modify overlapping code.
lessons.practice: Assign separate file or subsystem ownership and define integration contracts first.

lessons.title: Track decisions and changes
lessons.principle: Plans evolve as evidence emerges.
lessons.practice: Update the plan when a discovered constraint changes sequence, scope, or design.

lessons.title: Re-plan after failures
lessons.principle: Repeated patching around a failed approach wastes context and creates complexity.
lessons.practice: Return to the model of the problem when evidence contradicts the original plan.

lessons.title: End with a verification phase
lessons.principle: Implementation is not the final plan item.
lessons.practice: Reserve a final step for full validation, diff review, documentation, and residual-risk assessment.

codeExamples.snippet:
1. Reproduce current bug — verify with failing test.
2. Fix service logic — run focused unit tests.
3. Update API adapter — run integration tests.
4. Verify user flow — run browser test.
5. Review final diff.

Phase 1: additive schema
Phase 2: dual-compatible app
Phase 3: backfill
Phase 4: switch reads
Phase 5: remove legacy column

paths.title: Architecture & System Design
paths.description: Use AI without surrendering architectural coherence, boundaries, data ownership, and long-term changeability.

lessons.title: Start with system boundaries
lessons.principle: Architecture begins by deciding what belongs together and what should remain separate.
lessons.practice: Identify users, external systems, trust boundaries, data stores, and major components.

lessons.title: Prefer simple architecture
lessons.principle: Complexity has ongoing cognitive and operational cost.
lessons.practice: Use the least complex design that satisfies current requirements and credible near-term needs.

lessons.title: Define module responsibilities
lessons.principle: Overlapping ownership produces coupling and duplicated rules.
lessons.practice: Give each module one clear responsibility and explicit public interfaces.

lessons.title: Keep domain rules centralized
lessons.principle: Duplicated business logic diverges over time.
lessons.practice: Place authoritative rules in a domain or service layer reusable by all entry points.

lessons.title: Separate policy from mechanism
lessons.principle: Policy changes more often than low-level mechanisms.
lessons.practice: Keep authorization, retry, routing, and business decisions configurable or isolated from implementation plumbing.

lessons.title: Design explicit interfaces
lessons.principle: Hidden coupling makes AI-generated changes unpredictable.
lessons.practice: Use typed contracts, schemas, and narrow APIs between components.

lessons.title: Control dependency direction
lessons.principle: Cycles make systems difficult to test and replace.
lessons.practice: Make lower-level modules independent of higher-level orchestration and UI concerns.

lessons.title: Choose state ownership deliberately
lessons.principle: Duplicated or ambiguous state causes synchronization bugs.
lessons.practice: Define one authoritative owner for each piece of mutable state.

lessons.title: Distinguish synchronous and asynchronous work
lessons.principle: Not every operation belongs in a request-response path.
lessons.practice: Move long, retryable, or fan-out work to durable asynchronous processing where appropriate.

lessons.title: Design idempotent operations
lessons.principle: Retries are normal in distributed systems.
lessons.practice: Use stable identifiers and idempotency keys for side-effecting operations that may be repeated.

lessons.title: Design failure boundaries
lessons.principle: One failing dependency should not always collapse the entire system.
lessons.practice: Use timeouts, circuit breaking, queues, isolation, or graceful degradation based on impact.

lessons.title: Model consistency requirements
lessons.principle: Strong consistency is costly and not always necessary.
lessons.practice: State which invariants require transactions and where eventual consistency is acceptable.

lessons.title: Design for observability
lessons.principle: Opaque architecture is hard to operate.
lessons.practice: Preserve request or job correlation across component boundaries and emit meaningful telemetry.

lessons.title: Avoid premature microservices
lessons.principle: Network boundaries add deployment, consistency, latency, and ownership complexity.
lessons.practice: Split services only when organizational or scaling boundaries justify the operational cost.

lessons.title: Use architecture decision records
lessons.principle: Consequential choices need durable rationale.
lessons.practice: Record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, and reversal conditions for major architecture decisions.

lessons.title: Protect public contracts
lessons.principle: Internal refactors should not accidentally break consumers.
lessons.practice: Version or evolve external APIs and events compatibly.

lessons.title: Plan capacity assumptions
lessons.principle: Architecture should match expected load and growth.
lessons.practice: Estimate traffic, storage, concurrency, and hot-path behavior before introducing scaling mechanisms.

lessons.title: Minimize shared mutable infrastructure
lessons.principle: Shared tables, caches, or globals create invisible coupling.
lessons.practice: Use clear ownership and access patterns for shared resources.

lessons.title: Review architecture after implementation
lessons.principle: Generated code can drift from an approved design.
lessons.practice: Inspect dependencies, boundaries, and data flow after the agent finishes, not just the feature output.

lessons.title: Optimize for change
lessons.principle: Good architecture makes likely future changes local and understandable.
lessons.practice: Choose boundaries around stable domain concepts rather than around accidental current file structure.

codeExamples.snippet:
ADR-012: Keep billing in the modular monolith
Context: one team, shared transaction boundary
Decision: no new service
Revisit when ownership or scaling boundaries diverge
